=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review for Wattlebridge (Buyer)

## Bottom line

The Seller's package is not a fair and balanced starting point. It combines a low general cap, a high threshold, a short time limit, a broad disclosure of the entire data room, and an anti-sandbagging clause. Together these would leave Wattlebridge with almost no warranty recourse for the risks already identified in the Seller's own disclosure letter. Known risks are being handled by "to be resolved later," "reasonable endeavours," "not expected to be material," or "ordinary course," with no price protection or specific indemnity.

I'd reject the "FINAL / not to be re-opened" framing. The principal-level agreement it refers to is not something Wattlebridge has confirmed, and the market-context claims are unsourced assertions. We should test them against our own precedent and any comparables we can verify, not accept them.

## Key departures and pushback

**1. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Disclosure Letter 1.1-1.2; Schedule 7)**
- *Concern:* Disclosing "every fact" in the data room as at 5pm 22 September 2026, plus all public registers, would disclose almost anything a warranty claim could rely on. Warranties would be hollow.
- *Pushback:* Delete the general disclosure. Allow only specific disclosure against specific warranties, with reasonable particularity. Data room documents are disclosed only where they are fairly disclosed in the letter itself. Public register searches are not deemed disclosure except as expressly listed.

**2. Buyer knowledge / anti-sandbagging (Clause 8.3)**
- *Concern:* This bars claims for anything Wattlebridge or its advisers knew or could discover from the data room or public records. Combined with clause 1.1, this is effectively a total bar.
- *Pushback:* Insist on a pro-sandbagging clause: Wattlebridge's knowledge does not affect its rights. Specific indemnities must apply regardless of knowledge in every case. Australian law on this point is not settled by default, so the position needs to be express. NSW counsel should confirm the drafting.

**3. General liability cap (Clause 12.1: 20%, AUD 4.8m)**
- *Concern:* 20% is the top of the range the Seller cites, and it is set against a deal with known, quantified exposures. Known cash-type items already total about AUD 4.13m (Riverlark AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 420k, Ironquay AUD 180k, Sandbar renewals AUD 330k), before any unquantified privacy, lease, Mossvale or tax exposure.
- *Pushback:* Seek a cap of at least 30-50% for general warranties, with fundamental warranties and tax at 100% of price. Known items should not rely on the warranty cap at all (see point 9).

**4. Thresholds (Clause 12.2: AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k excess-only basket, about 1.04% of price)**
- *Concern:* An excess-only basket means the first AUD 250k of claims is unrecoverable. With a de minimis of AUD 25k, small related claims are also excluded and may not aggregate.
- *Pushback:* Reduce the basket to about 0.5% of price, make it a "tipping" basket (once crossed, recovery is from the first dollar), and aggregate related claims arising from the same facts. The de minimis should not apply to fundamental warranties, tax or specific indemnities.

**5. Time limits (Clauses 12.3 and 13: 18 months for general warranties; uniform application to all claims)**
- *Concern:* 18 months may expire before FY27 tax returns, the first audit cycle after Completion, or the outcome of the privacy investigation and Bluefen revenue performance are known. Applying the same limit to fundamental and title claims is not appropriate.
- *Pushback:* General warranties at 24-36 months. Tax claims until 60 days after the expiry of the relevant ATO amendment period. Title, capacity and authority at six years (the NSW contract limitation period, subject to verification). Specific indemnities should run for a period matched to the underlying risk, for example until the regulator's limitation period has passed.

**6. Fundamental and title warranties on general terms (Fundamental / Title)**
- *Concern:* Applying general caps and time limits to title and capacity for "administrative simplicity" would cap title risk at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m share purchase.
- *Pushback:* Title, capacity, authority, share capital and the Seller's power to sell carve out of the cap (up to 100% of price), the basket and the de minimis.

**7. Exclusive remedy, non-reliance and limitations applied to "all Claims of any nature" (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)**
- *Concern:* This would catch fraud and specific indemnities. Excluding fraud from a contract is generally not enforceable in any event, and an express carve-out avoids argument.
- *Pushback:* Carve out fraud, fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities from all limitations and exclusive-remedy language. Non-reliance should carve out fraud and the express warranties in the SPA.

**8. Conditions and consents**
- **Bluefen (Clauses 3 and 6.3):** The Seller will use reasonable endeavours and deem the consent satisfied on receipt of "the counterparty's written consent." Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m). Deeming satisfaction is not acceptable. Push for: consent as a condition precedent in its final form, with conditions in clause 11.3 satisfied or waived by Wattlebridge; a longstop date; a walk-right if not obtained; and no price-neutral completion without it.
- **Riverlark (Clauses 2 and 7):** A release "following Completion" means Wattlebridge would fund the price and then wait for discharge. This is inconsistent with debt-free/cash-free. Require a payoff letter, payment of the AUD 3.2m out of the price at Completion, and PPSR discharge (and any other security release) at or before Completion.
- **Mossvale, office lease:** The Seller's disclaimer that consent is not "legally required" (clause 1.4) is not enough. Obtain written confirmation from the landlord and Mossvale that no consent is needed, or obtain consent as a condition. This is a point for Australian property and commercial counsel to confirm against the lease and the Mossvale agreement.

**9. Specific risks: require specific indemnities (not warranties)**

Because the Seller has disclosed these matters, Wattlebridge cannot rely on warranties for them. Each should be a pound-for-pound, first-dollar indemnity, outside the basket and general cap, with an appropriate retention or escrow:

- **Bluefen consent and revenue:** loss arising from failure to obtain consent or from termination or repricing under clause 11.2/11.3 of the Bluefen agreement.
- **Riverlark:** any amount outstanding at Completion beyond the funds flow payoff, plus enforcement costs.
- **Ironquay SOW3 (Clause 11.1):** the current indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. It should cover all SOW3 and related fees, any IP ownership claim, third-party claims over the Project Materials and any transfer defect. The AUD 180k open amount should be paid, or a confirmatory assignment delivered, before Completion as a condition.
- **Employee bonuses (DD-005):** AUD 420k is not in the funds flow. Under cash-free/debt-free, these are debt-like items and should either be deducted from price or borne by the Seller, including payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs, which the disclosure does not address.
- **Privacy/export incident (DD-006, Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6):** The Seller calls this "not expected to be material," but the disclosure states that the investigation is preliminary, the scope is unknown (around 1,240 records with personal information), and it is not known whether unauthorised access occurred or whether notification is required. Require: a forensic investigation completed or scoped before Completion at Seller cost; a specific indemnity for notification costs, regulatory investigations and penalties under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), and third-party claims; a privacy compliance warranty; and a retention or escrow sized to the likely exposure. Australian privacy counsel should assess the notification obligations.
- **Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330k):** Calling these "ordinary course" is not established. Require the contracts, confirm whether each is terminable and whether it is a pre-Completion commitment, and treat any unavoidable amount as a price adjustment or Seller cost.
- **Tax:** The Seller considers tax warranties "settled." They are not. Require a standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity, uncapped up to price, and tax warranties with the extended time limit above.

**10. Funds flow**
- *Concern:* The Seller says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics," but it omits the AUD 420k bonuses and does not show the Riverlark payoff.
- *Pushback:* Require a full, reconciled funds flow showing the price, debt, debt-like items (including the bonuses and related payroll costs), cash and working capital adjustments, and the Riverlark payoff, before signing.

**11. Title (DD-012)**
- *Concern:* The share register shows Harbourglass as holder of 100% of the shares, but that is the Seller's source, not Wattlebridge's verification.
- *Pushback:* Obtain a current ASIC company extract, the original share certificates, a PPSR search over the shares, confirmation of no encumbrances, and a Seller warranty of title that is a fundamental warranty with the carve-outs above.

## Recommendations (summary)

1. Reject the "FINAL" framing and the unsourced market claims. Confirm internally that the principals have not agreed these terms.
2. Delete general data room and public register disclosure. Allow specific disclosure only.
3. Replace the anti-sandbagging clause with a pro-sandbagging clause.
4. Raise the general cap to 30-50% of price. Set fundamental warranties and tax at 100%.
5. Lower the basket to about 0.5%, make it tipping, and reduce or remove the de minimis for key claims.
6. Extend general time limits to 24-36 months, with six years for title and tax tied to the ATO period.
7. Carve out fraud, fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities from all exclusions and limitations.
8. Make Bluefen consent a condition precedent with a longstop date and walk-right. Remove the "deemed satisfied" language.
9. Require payoff of Riverlark at Completion from the price, with PPSR discharge.
10. Convert every disclosed known risk (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy incident, supplier renewals, lease, Mossvale, tax) into a specific indemnity, with escrow or retention where appropriate.
11. Require a reconciled funds flow including the AUD 420k bonuses and related payroll costs.
12. Complete the title verification steps for the shares before signing.

## Caveats

- I have reviewed only the Seller's summary and disclosure letter, not the full SPA, the underlying data room documents (DD-002 to DD-012), or the Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, lease and Mossvale agreements. Several points depend on what those documents actually say.
- Statutory references (Privacy Act obligations, limitation periods, PPSA discharge, ATO amendment periods, payroll tax) should be confirmed by NSW and Australian specialist counsel. I have not checked current rates or the current state of the law.
- The figures in this note are taken from the Seller's documents and have not been verified against the data room.
